newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end down on qtr-end selling.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end down on qtr-end selling.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended lower after a late push to new session highs abruptly fizzled.

Traders linked the late drop to quarter-end selling pressure. Some independent S&P 500 futures traders who got long anticipating institutional buying at the end of the second quarter were forced to liquidate when the support did not materialize, floor brokers said.
One U.S. brokerage house sold about 500 S&P futures contracts at the highs to spark the turnaround, traders said.
Just before the final sell-off, S&P 500 futures had pushed to fresh session highs following the 1400 CDT close of bond futures trading.
Both bonds and stocks spent most of the day drifting up from morning lows hit after a pair of strong U.S. economic reports surprised financial market participants.
After bonds closed, September S&P index futures extended the rebound, climbing back above unchanged and setting a fresh high of 901.80 before diving sharply into the close.
Earlier, stock index futures were pummeled along with bonds after the release of the June Chicago purchasing managers' index and May U.S. new home sales. Both reports exceeded analysts' expectations.
The Chicago purchasers' business barometer rose to 61.5 from 56.8 in May. Traders had expected a rise to 57.5.

May U.S. single-family home sales climbed 7.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 825,000 units, the largest increase since November, outstripping expectations for a more modest rise to 786,000.

On Tuesday, the National Association of Purchasing Management releases its June data. Traders said the report probably would have less influence on prices than the Chicago survey because of the Federal Open Market Committee under way. The FOMC begins a two-day meeting Tuesday morning.
On Thursday, which is a shortened trading session for index futures, U.S. June employment data are set for release. Markets are closed Friday for the Independence Day holiday.
Nonfarm payrolls are seen rising 222,000, from a 138,000 rise in May, and the unemployment rate is seen unchanged at 4.8 percent.

September S&P 500s ended 6.65 points lower at 890.25, Nasdaq 100s were 8.65 lower at 966.50, Nikkei 225 index futures eased 30.0 to 20,595.0 and Midcap 400s fell 1.25 points to 289.60. ((--Derivatives Desk: 312-408-8750)) email:derivatives@reuters.com
